releases.title: California Opens New Workforce Pell Grant Application Portal for Institutions to Determine Career Training Program Eligibility
releases.body:
SACRAMENTO, Calif., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The California Student Aid Commission (CSAC) today announced the launching of the state application portal for the new federal Workforce Pell (WFP) Grant Program. The WFP state application portal will open on October 21 for higher education institutions and career technical education providers to apply for state authorization to participate in the program.

Articulated in California Senate Bill 135, on behalf of the Governor, CSAC is the designated California state agency to determine whether an institution's short-term program meets the state and federal program requirements, in consultation with the California Workforce Development Board and the Labor and Workforce Development Agency. After a short-term program has been deemed eligible, institutions submit the information directly to the U.S. Department of Education (ED) for review and final approval. The ED will notify institutions of their eligibility to participate in the WFP and allow eligible students to begin accessing these new federal Workforce Pell Grants disbursed through the campus financial aid office.

The WFP grant represents one of the most significant expansions of federal financial aid in decades. WFP is designed to expand financial aid opportunities for students pursuing short-term, high-quality workforce training programs that lead directly to high-skill, high-wage, or in-demand occupations. Completed 100 days since the passage of the state budget, the state portal marks a significant milestone in California's implementation efforts and begins the process of identifying programs across the state.

Institutions and programs seeking eligibility are strongly encouraged to participate in CSAC's Webinar on October 20., California Get Ready: A Pathway to a Successful Workforce Pell Grant Application will cover the portal requirements in detail including a technical guide to address federally required formular and state eligibility requirements. 

Expanding Access to In-Demand Career Technical Education

The portal launch by the California Student Aid Commission allows for institutions to apply to be eligible starting in the 2026-27 academic year. For students, this means that eligible students enrolled in approved short-term career technical education (CTE) programs can soon begin receiving federal WFP Grants. Designed for programs running between 150 and 599 clock hours (8 to 15 weeks), WFP helps learners quickly gain specialized skills for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers.

Unlike traditional Pell Grants, WFP can also be used by students who already hold a bachelor's degree (provided they do not hold a graduate degree). Coupled with the recent changes to Cal Grant C, which now includes programs as short as 8 weeks; students will be able to stack both Cal Grant C and Workforce Pell Grant, creating powerful new reskilling and upskilling pathways for California's adult workforce.

Leaders Across California on Workforce Pell Grant Program:

"California is building more pathways to good-paying careers — and making sure opportunity isn't limited by where you come from or whether you have a four-year degree," said Governor Gavin Newsom . "Through Workforce Pell, we're expanding financial aid opportunities and helping Californians move faster into in-demand jobs, build new skills, and get ahead in our growing economy."

"Ensuring our workforce development programs are directly tied to regional labor market needs is essential for California's economic future," said Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin. "With the signing of AB 1534, the state authorization process safeguards student investments by prioritizing high-quality programs that deliver true economic value, higher wages, and strong career outcomes for our workforce."

"By establishing Workforce Pell as an option for California students, we are chipping away at the college affordability barriers adult learners face in every region of our state," said Dr. Daisy Gonzales, Executive Director of the California Student Aid Commission . "The California Student Aid Commission supports colleges and universities, who provide high- quality, short-term career technical education and skills training, and with Workforce Pell as an option, state and federal aid will open new doors for adult learners and working learners. The portal opening is California's spirit of innovation to strengthen workforce pipelines by centering financial aid as a catalyst for economic mobility in our state." "Short-term credentials are vital vehicles for rapid social and economic mobility," said Dr. Sonya Christian, Chancellor of the California Community Colleges . "The launch of Phase One allows our community colleges to align state and federal support around targeted workforce programs, empowering more students to gain immediate industry-recognized skills and transition into sustainable, living-wage careers." "At Compton College, we see firsthand how targeted, short-term training can transform lives and lift entire communities," said Dr. Keith Curry, President/CEO of Compton College . "Workforce Pell removes significant financial barriers for working adults and many of our students who need flexible, accelerated options to gain career-ready credentials without taking on debt, or for many of our students, additional debt." "Home care and child care providers across California rely on continuous skill-building to adapt, advance, and better serve our communities," said Doug Moore, Executive Director of United Domestic Workers (UDW/AFSCME Local 3930) . "Expanding federal Pell support to short-term workforce training provides working people and adult learners a vital, realistic bridge to higher wages and career advancement."

Student Requirements

To be eligible for a Workforce Pell Grant, students must:

  • Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and meet federal Pell Grant eligibility requirements.
  • Hold a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
  • Be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen.
  • Not be currently enrolled in a bachelor's or higher-level degree program.
  • Enroll in an approved short-term workforce program at a participating institution.

Institutional Application & Letters of Intent

To disburse or advertise Workforce Pell funds, institutions must secure state authorization from CSAC, the California State Governor, and the U.S. Department of Education.

  • Portal Submission: Eligible institutions seeking program authorization can submit program data through the new CSAC program portal launching October 21.
  • Letters of Interest (By December 15, 2026): Institutions seeking eligibility that do not have existing data-sharing agreements with the Employment Development Department (EDD) pursuant to Unemployment Insurance Code Section 1095 must submit a letter of interest to CSAC and the Office of Cradle-to-Career Data on or before December 15, 2026 (and annually thereafter).
    • Letter Requirements: Must indicate the name and number of programs, the targeted high-demand sectors aligned with state EDC 69871 lists, and average class sizes. Applications for these institutions will be processed following statutory updates governing equivalent data sharing.

The California Student Aid Commission currently serves over 2.2 million students and administers over $3.9 billion of student financial aid programs and services, including the Cal Grant, the Middle Class Scholarship, and the California Dream Act Application. The Commission serves as a resource for policymakers and the public on college affordability and financing issues, and advocates for policy changes to eliminate cost as a barrier to any qualified California student pursuing a higher education. Visit our website at www.csac.ca.gov or follow us on social media by clicking on our Link Tree.

releases.title: SWC Spotlights neXus During America's Safe Schools Week
releases.body:
NEWBURGH, Ind., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In recognition of America's Safe Schools Week (October 19-23, 2026), South Western Communications (SWC) is highlighting neXus, a platform that streamlines school safety by integrating fragmented security systems into a single interface for faster response. As school districts nationwide increase their focus on campus safety and security, SWC's neXus empowers administrators to see real-time alerts, automate critical response workflows, and take immediate action when seconds count.

neXus' interactive 3D map brings together people, places, devices, alerts, and predefined response actions onto a single pane of glass. It integrates with technologies schools already own including access control, video surveillance, API-powered weapon detection, duress alerts, vape detection, intercoms, emergency notifications, and more.

See neXus in action in our 90-second animated demonstration.

"As schools across the country assess their safety measures during America's Safe Schools Week, the ability to turn existing technologies into a coordinated response is increasingly important," said Todd Lucy, SWC President. "neXus builds on SWC's 50-year legacy of safety, reliability, and strong local partnerships by giving schools a clearer operational picture when every second matters. It reflects our commitment to innovation, customer support, and helping communities strengthen school safety without walking away from the systems they already trust."

Building on SWC's commitment, the real-world impact of neXus is best illustrated by education leaders who have experienced its benefits firsthand.

Dr. Scott McWilliams, a recently retired superintendent for a Kansas school district and now the Business Development Manager for neXus, shared his experience: "Having served as a superintendent for 11 years and as a member of our district's school safety committee, I can say without hesitation that neXus transformed the way we approached school safety. Its ability to integrate seamlessly with our existing technology delivered significant value while helping us maximize limited budget resources."

Dr. McWilliams continued: "Most importantly, the interactive 3D mapping platform unified our security systems into a single, real-time operational view, providing instant access to the critical information needed to make informed decisions when every second matters."

Key Features of neXus

  • Integrate Existing Systems: Leverages the systems schools already own, with no rip-and-replace required, through API and cloud-based technology, saving districts time and money.
  • Visualize the Campus in 3D: Provides interactive, state-of-the-art 3D mapping with real-time device and alert overlays, thus reducing response times.
  • Automate Response Workflows: Enables schools to customize automatic responses to real-time events, such as lockdowns, emergency notifications, contacting authorities. and other predefined actions.
  • Support Compliance Requirements: Helps schools support Alyssa's Law and related safety mandates by integrating silent panic alarms, emergency notifications, and law enforcement connectivity.

Alongside its advanced technology, SWC's collaborative approach ensures districts receive expert guidance and support throughout implementation.

Dr. McWilliams emphasized the value of working with SWC:

"Beyond the technology itself, the experience, expertise, and unwavering support provided by the SWC team were exceptional. Their role as trusted advisors to our school safety team brought invaluable insight and guidance throughout the process, helping us strengthen our preparedness and create a safer environment for students, staff, and the entire school community."

SWC operates locally in Alabama, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Missouri, and Tennessee. We collaborate with a trusted network of channel partners to deliver neXus to school districts nationwide. This partnership-driven approach ensures that schools across the country can access, implement, and maximize the benefits of neXus, regardless of their location.

Media interviews with SWC leadership and neXus subject-matter experts are available, along with product visuals and guided demonstrations for reporters covering school safety, education technology, emergency communications, and campus operations. For a deeper dive or to schedule an in-person or virtual demonstration, visit www.swc.net/neXus or contact marketing@swc.net.

About SWC

Founded in 1976, South Western Communications (SWC) is an integrator of life safety, security, communications, and critical workflow solutions serving education, healthcare, commercial, government, and detention customers. With nine offices across eight states, SWC helps organizations connect the systems, people, and information that matter most. SWC has been part of the Koch Enterprises, Inc. family since 2006, offering customers the strength and stability of a long-standing, diversified private company. Learn more at www.swc.net.

releases.body:
A Guinness World Record holder, a free exhibition, and 550 young Marylanders under one theme: You Can

BALTIMORE, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On Friday, October 30, 550 high school seniors, college students, and early-career professionals will fill the Gordon Center for Performing Arts in Owings Mills for NextGen Summit. Built around the theme "You Can," the one-day event gives young Marylanders what they say they're missing most: funding, connections, and a clear path to their purpose and career goals.

The opportunity is specific. Ten young founders, 25 and under, will pitch live to a panel of business and community leaders, and the top three will share $10,000 to launch their ideas. The public votes one finalist onto the stage. Founders can apply through October 20 at nextgensummit.us. A free exhibition puts young entrepreneurs in front of attendees, customers, mentors, and potential partners.

Speakers:

  • Tisha Edwards, President & CEO of the Maryland Bankers Association and former Chief of Staff on Governor Wes Moore's campaign, on building a career in banking, business, and leadership
  • Tunde Onakoya, Guinness World Record holder and founder of Chess in Slums Africa, who turned a single chessboard into a program that has reached more than 10,000 children
  • Kennedy Ekezie, Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree and founder of Kippa, who started his first organization at 16

The day runs on TED-style talks, podcast-style conversations, and audience discussion and ends with every attendee writing down their next step.

"Every generation is told what is wrong with it. In one day, NextGen Summit will show these young people the greatness already in them. This may be the generation that preserves the future," said Pastor Deji Olubusi, Chairman, NextGen Summit.

DETAILS

Date: Friday, October 30, 2026

Exhibition: 2:00 PM | Main Stage: 4:15 to 7:00 PM

Location: Gordon Center for Performing Arts, Owings Mills, MD

Tickets: $20, or $10 each for groups of three or more.

Registration required at nextgensummit.us.

ABOUT NEXTGEN SUMMIT

NextGen Summit is a Maryland platform that puts funding, connections, and direction in front of rising leaders, built on one message: You Can.

releases.title: CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus Name Jim Wilson CEO to Lead Next Phase of Growth and Transformation
releases.body:
Experienced technology and services executive to build on the combined organization's strengths in managed services, institutional leadership, and operational transformation.

AUSTIN, Texas, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus, a comprehensive services partner to higher education, today announced the appointment of Jim Wilson as Chief Executive Officer. Wilson joined the company on Sept. 1. The company is backed by Atlantic Street Capital ("ASC").

Wilson is an accomplished executive with extensive experience leading, scaling, and transforming technology and professional services organizations. Throughout his career, he has focused on building high-performing teams, strengthening client partnerships, driving operational excellence, and delivering measurable business outcomes. He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of RedHelm, President of Ntiva, and Chief Operating Officer of Integration Partners.

Wilson succeeds Liz Murphy, who led CampusWorks for 15 years, and Jody Glubke, who co-founded Dynamic Campus and led the organization for 24 years. Both leaders played instrumental roles in establishing the organizations' deep institutional relationships, higher education expertise, and commitment to client success. Murphy and Glubke will remain engaged as strategic advisors, supporting continuity as the combined organization grows.

"We're excited to welcome Jim as CEO of CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus. Jim brings the managed services experience and vision we need as we enter this next chapter of growth for the combined organization," said Paul Sun, Partner at ASC. "Jim's focus on building trusted, lasting relationships with the institutions we serve is central to that vision. I'm confident he's the right leader to build upon the strong foundation we have in place, and we look forward to partnering with him to drive continued growth in an ever-changing higher education landscape as we help our institutional partners deliver on their missions."

Wilson's appointment follows the merger of CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus earlier this year, bringing together complementary strengths in institutional leadership, technology, finance, human resources, data, and managed services. The combined organization helps colleges and universities manage growing operational complexity, improve institutional performance, and build lasting capacity. Under Wilson's leadership, the company will deepen client partnerships, integrate its capabilities, and expand its impact across higher education.

"I'm honored to lead an organization with such a clear purpose and a longstanding commitment to the institutions we serve," said Wilson. "Colleges and universities are navigating extraordinary change, and their success requires more than technology alone. It takes exceptional people, strong leadership, connected data, and the ability to translate strategy into action. By bringing together the expertise and capabilities of CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus, we have a tremendous opportunity to help institutional leaders strengthen performance and advance the missions that matter most to their students and communities."

About CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus

CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus have joined forces to become a comprehensive managed services and transformation partner for higher education. Together, the organizations help colleges and universities strengthen institutional performance, extend operational capacity, reduce risk, and navigate complex change.

Combining deep higher education expertise with a vendor-neutral approach, the organization provides institutional leadership, managed services, technology, enterprise applications, finance, human resources, data, and operational transformation capabilities. Through trusted partnerships and a commitment to measurable results, CampusWorks and Dynamic Campus help institutions build stronger operations and advance their missions.

For more information, visit www.campusworksinc.com and www.dynamiccampus.com.

About Atlantic Street Capital

Atlantic Street Capital is a private equity firm that invests in lower middle market companies poised for the next level of growth. The firm targets entrepreneurial management partners and fundamentally sound companies between $4 million and $25 million of EBITDA that will benefit from capital investment and ASC's value-added strategic and operational support. As a result, ASC works closely with management to unlock their business' underlying value and help them succeed. For more information, visit www.atlanticstreetcapital.com.

releases.title: Jaguar Promise Expands Access to Higher Education at A&M-San Antonio
releases.body:
SAN ANTONIO, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As Texas A&M University-San Antonio's enrollment reached 7,697 students in Fall 2026, including a record 1,322 first-time-in-college students, the University is working to ensure that the cost of higher education does not stand in the way of opportunity.

That commitment is reflected in Jaguar Promise, a scholarship program designed to make college more affordable for eligible Texas residents, including transfer students and adult learners. With 60% of A&M-San Antonio students eligible for federal Pell Grants, the program plays an important role in helping students pursue their degrees with less financial burden.

As a last-dollar scholarship, Jaguar Promise, which launched in 2024, covers remaining tuition and mandatory fees after eligible federal, state and institutional financial aid is applied. Participants also receive a $300-per-semester book stipend.

Participation continues to grow. The number of first-year students receiving Jaguar Promise funding increased 21% over the previous year. Among first-year participants, enrollment grew 48% among Early College High School graduates and 9% among students who graduated in the top 10% to 35% of their high school class.

"Jaguar Promise has made a meaningful difference in my college experience," said Student Body President Caroleena Mancilla. "Knowing that my tuition and fees are covered has allowed me to focus more on my education, leadership opportunities and personal growth instead of constantly worrying about how I will pay for college. That support has opened the door to experiences that are helping me grow both personally and professionally."

Beyond helping students afford college, Jaguar Promise supports the University's broader efforts to promote student persistence and degree completion. Program requirements include maintaining a minimum 12-credit-hour course load each semester and meeting established GPA and academic progress standards.

The University is also working with Alamo Colleges District through its Promise-to-Promise partnership, which helps eligible students transition from an associate degree to a bachelor's degree while pursuing a more affordable, debt-free path to graduation.

"Affordability can make the difference between whether students simply aspire to attend college and whether they can turn that aspiration into a degree," said Brandy McLelland, vice president for enrollment management. "The growing participation in Jaguar Promise reflects the importance of providing students and families with a clear, affordable path to higher education. By reducing financial barriers and supporting students as they progress toward graduation, we are advancing our commitment to access and student success."

That commitment extends to the University's expanding academic offerings, which are designed to connect students with emerging career opportunities across San Antonio and South Texas. In Fall 2026, A&M-San Antonio launched its first doctoral program, the Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership. The University will also introduce a Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Sciences in Fall 2027, with programs in electrical engineering, healthcare administration and management, computer engineering, and construction engineering technology planned for subsequent years.

For President Salvador Hector Ochoa, the University's growth reflects a broader commitment to expanding opportunity while responding to the needs of the region.

"As A&M-San Antonio grows, our responsibility remains the same: to open doors to higher education and help more students achieve their goals," Ochoa said. "We are expanding academic opportunities and strengthening our research enterprise while keeping affordability and student success at the center of our mission. Our true measure of success is when we create lasting opportunities for the students, families and communities we serve."

releases.title: Mentor Collective Launches Flash Mentoring to Close the Career Readiness Gap in Higher Education
releases.body:
New flexible mentoring model gives every student access to alumni expertise, complementing Mentor Collective's Structured Mentoring programs

BOSTON, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mentor Collective, higher education's preferred edtech platform for student mentorship, announced the launch of Flash Mentoring, a new, purposeful model built around focused, single-session conversations between students and alumni. Flash Mentoring joins Mentor Collective's existing Structured Mentoring model to support the full arc of the student journey, from belonging to employability, on one platform.

Higher education institutions are under unprecedented pressure to demonstrate career readiness, workforce outcomes, and degree ROI. Many students, including first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented students, still lack access to the professional networks that open doors, and not every student is looking for, or has time for, a long-term match. Mentor Collective meets students right where they are. With Flash Mentoring, every student has a low-barrier way to build real-world social capital on their own terms: whenever they need it, and as often as they need it, with no long-term commitment required.

"Every student's path looks different, and their support should too," said Patrick Garayta, Chief Executive Officer of Mentor Collective. "Some students want an ongoing relationship with a peer mentor. Others need the right person with the right experience for one purposeful conversation. Flash Mentoring and Structured Mentoring are built for exactly that reason, and together, they mean no students' needs will fall through the cracks."

Flash Mentoring is also designed with alumni in mind. Traditional engagement strategies, from reunions to newsletters to committee service, reach only a small fraction of a given alumni base. Flash offers a flexible, time-boxed way for alumni to give back in a single conversation, activating graduates who would never respond to a longer commitment. At the same time, advancement and alumni relations teams gain a new, trackable form of engagement to bring to leadership.

"Career offices and advancement teams keep telling us the same thing: their networks are bigger than their engagement numbers show," said Jennifer Kious, Director of Marketing at Mentor Collective. "Flash Mentoring is specifically built to reach the alumni who are typically disengaged. Every conversation becomes data our partners can use to tell a clearer story about alumni engagement and student outcomes."

Flash Mentoring gives every student a low-barrier way to build that access: a focused conversation with an alum around a specific question or goal, without the long-term commitment of a traditional mentoring program. For alumni, it offers a meaningful, flexible way to give back on their own schedule. For institutions, every conversation becomes a logged, reportable data point that strengthens the case for continued investment in student success.

Many students, including first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented students, still lack access to the professional networks that open doors, and not every student is looking for, or has time for, a long-term match. Flash Mentoring gives every student a low-barrier way to build real-world social capital on their own terms: a single, focused conversation with an alum around a specific question or goal, whenever they need it, and as often as they need it, with no long-term commitment required.

Flash Mentoring is available now to all higher education institutions, on its own or alongside Structured Mentoring, through the same co-branded experience and reporting dashboard partners already use to track student outcomes.

Mentor Collective expects Flash Mentoring to help partner institutions nationwide expand access to career readiness support, close equity gaps in social capital, and give alumni a meaningful, low-lift way to stay connected to their alma mater.

To learn more about Flash Mentoring, visit mentorcollective.org.

Connect with Mentor Collective on social media:

LinkedIn: www.linkedin.com/company/mentorcollective

About Mentor Collective

Mentor Collective is an education technology provider that drives student enrollment, retention, and career readiness through research-backed, scalable mentorship solutions. The company's mission is to ensure every learner realizes their full potential through connections, confidence, and support—not by chance, but by design. Mentor Collective enables institutions to embed personalized mentorship into the fabric of the learner experience, strengthening belonging, closing social capital gaps, and accelerating career readiness. Backed by over a decade of results, Mentor Collective supports more than one million participants across 200+ partnerships.

releases.title: The Inner Circle acknowledges Dr. Joseph G. R. Martinez as a Pinnacle Professional of The Year
releases.body:
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M., Oct. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Prominently featured in The Inner Circle, Dr. Joseph G. R. Martinez is acknowledged as a Pinnacle Professional of The Year for his contributions to Mathematics Education and Student Success.

Dr. Joseph G. R. Martinez has built a distinguished career in higher education, dedicating nearly four decades to teaching and advancing mathematics education. As a retired faculty member of the University of New Mexico, he is recognized for his commitment to student success and his ability to make complex mathematical concepts accessible to learners at all levels.

Dr. Martinez specialized in mathematics education, graduate statistics, calculus, and algebra, with a particular focus on reducing math anxiety. His teaching approach emphasized patience and step by step instruction, helping students build confidence and develop a deeper understanding of mathematical principles. His methods have inspired many students to pursue further studies and careers in mathematics.

He earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Education and Mathematics, with concentrations in mathematics education and educational psychology, from the University of New Mexico in 1980. His academic background provided a strong foundation for his work in both teaching and research design.

Throughout his career, Dr. Martinez taught at the University of New Mexico until his retirement in 2012 and also held earlier teaching roles at the University of Albuquerque. Over the years, he became widely respected for his engaging teaching style and dedication to supporting student achievement.

In addition to his work in the classroom, Dr. Martinez is an accomplished author, having written eight books and more than 200 published articles. His book Math Without Fear, along with other works including those coauthored with his late wife Nancy, reflects his mission to make mathematics more approachable and less intimidating for students.

Dr. Martinez credits his wife, Nancy, as a key influence in refining his teaching philosophy and instructional methods. Her support and insight played an important role in shaping his approach to education.

Looking ahead, Dr. Martinez is exploring opportunities to expand his educational outreach, particularly within Orthodox Jewish communities. Guided by a philosophy that anyone can learn mathematics with the right support and instruction, he remains committed to sharing his knowledge and helping others overcome challenges in learning.

releases.title: ALPFA announces the 2026 Scholarship Recipients, investing in the next generation of student leaders
releases.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ALPFA proudly announced the recipients of its 2026 Student Scholarship Program during the 2026 ALPFA Convention, awarding $1.4 million to 334 students in recognition of their academic excellence, leadership, and commitment to making a lasting impact in their communities across North America. This year's scholarship recipients reflect the talent, resilience and ambition shaping the future of business, technology, healthcare, finance, public service and entrepreneurship. With awards ranging from $2,500 to $10,000, the program represents ALPFA's continued investment in expanding access to higher education and professional opportunity.

Join us in expanding pathways to education, opportunity and career growth for the next generation of leaders. Support ALPFA's continued investment in students and communities.

Impact in Action

The ALPFA 2026 Student Scholarship Program awarded $1.4 million to 334 students, representing 122 colleges and universities across 31 states. The recipients included 240 first-generation college students and 203 students across 52 Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs), highlighting the program's reach across institutions serving our communities nationwide.

A Commitment to Opportunity

"At ALPFA, we want every student to see a future where their culture and their career pull in the same direction where who they are becomes a source of strength in who they are becoming. These scholarships help create that future by expanding access to education, opportunity, relationships and experiences that can change the trajectory of a life. We are proudly rooted in Latino culture and open to all, building a community where people can learn from one another, lead authentically and use their success to create opportunity for the people who follow. When we invest in these students, we are investing in the leaders who will help build a better future for all of us." said Damian Rivera, President and CEO of ALPFA

The ALPFA Student Scholarship Program is designed to remove financial barriers to higher education while connecting students to a national network of mentors, corporate partners, and career development opportunities. Reflecting ALPFA's commitment to creating pathways to opportunity, the scholarship program welcomes students across all majors and backgrounds who meet application, academic and enrollment criteria. Beyond academic achievement, recipients are recognized for their leadership, service, resilience, and commitment to advancing their community.

"At ALPFA, investing in our students' education is a commitment to the dreams of our community," said Maria V. Fernandez, Student Programs Manager. "We see education as an accelerator, one that can transform the trajectory of a student's life and create an impact that reaches far beyond any single award. When we invest in them, we are also investing in the people they will mentor, the doors they will open, and the generations that will follow. That is how a scholarship becomes more than financial support. It becomes a lasting legacy of opportunity."

With more than 1,400 applications, the 2026 scholarship recipients represent a diverse group of emerging leaders bringing their own experiences, ambitions and perspectives to the next chapter of their academic and professional journeys. They are pursuing degrees across a wide range of disciplines, including business, engineering, healthcare, technology, and more, reflecting the strength and diversity of multicultural talent across undergraduate, graduate, and community college programs.

Meet the Scholars

Hear directly from some of our scholarship recipients and learn about their experiences here. 

Several recipients shared what receiving an ALPFA scholarship means to them:

"You have given me more than a scholarship—you have given me the confidence to push forward, knowing that I am not just building a career for myself, but a pathway for those who will follow in my footsteps." – Daniela Correa, Hult International Business School



"Beyond the financial support, this recognition serves as a reminder that hard work, perseverance, and community involvement matter. Through ALPFA, I have developed valuable leadership skills, built meaningful relationships, and gained access to opportunities that have shaped my career path. This scholarship motivates me to continue striving for excellence, give back to my community, and create opportunities for others who share similar aspirations." – Lorelys Alvarez, Lehman College CUNY

Creating Pathways for What's Next

The 2026 Student Scholarship Program was made possible through the generous support of our partners, whose commitment helped ALPFA award $1.4 million to 334 students. Their investment extends beyond financial support, helping scholars pursue their ambitions, build on their strengths and translate their potential into meaningful career impact.

This year, 8 scholarship recipients were also selected for fellowship opportunities, extending that investment through continued professional development, mentorship and career experiences. Together, these opportunities help prepare the next generation of professionals to contribute, lead and shape the future of the workforce.

Scholarships are one of the many ways ALPFA invests in the next generation of leaders. Through 270+ student chapters and 50+ professional chapters, ALPFA provides year-round access to career resources, mentorship, bootcamps, leadership development and a nationwide professional network. At the 2026 ALPFA Convention, 5,800+ attendees—including 3,200+ professionals, 2,600+ students, 370+ executives and 250+ speakers—came together, creating opportunities for students to connect with leading employers, expand their networks, build career-ready skills and take the next step in their professional journeys.

Learn more about our scholarship eligibility requirements and application criteria and fellowship opportunities designed to support students' continued professional development and career growth.

Join us in building pathways to opportunity and investing in the leaders of tomorrow. 

About ALPFA

Founded in 1972, ALPFA is the nation's leading professional association dedicated to empowering and developing leaders. With a nationwide network of professional and student chapters, ALPFA provides leadership development, career opportunities, mentorship, and community to professionals and students across every stage of their careers. Through strategic partnerships with leading organizations, ALPFA continues to create pathways for the next generation of leaders while advancing representation across every industry.

releases.title: American University Taps DC College Access Program to Expand Pathways to Opportunity for Local Students
releases.body:
Pioneering D.C. nonprofit welcomes its newest university partner, unlocking financial aid and wraparound services for college-ready students in the District

WASHINGTON, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The DC College Access Program (DC CAP), a nonprofit dedicated to eliminating the higher education achievement gap for Washington, D.C. students, announced American University as its newest university partner today. The collaboration will expand access to higher education pathways that change lives and strengthen communities in the nation's capital.

"Together with DC CAP, we're taking a critical next step toward closing the college opportunity gap for D.C. students. Washington, D.C. isn't just where American University is located, it's our home, and we have a responsibility to ensure that talented students across the District can see a path to an AU education," said Jeremy Lowe, interim vice president of Undergraduate Enrollment Management at American University. "Our partnership with DC CAP strengthens that commitment by helping more D.C. students obtain access, afford, and ultimately thrive in college."

American University joins DC CAP's broader network of University Partners, which provide eligible D.C. students with the support and structure they need to thrive in college, from application to degree completion. Students who participate in the University Partnerships program are more likely to persist through college than their peers: 85% of freshmen continue on to their sophomore year, and 57-100% graduate from college within five years, 3-5 times the national average, reducing the likelihood of accruing unnecessary educational debt and opening the door to greater economic and career opportunities.

As a DC CAP University Partner, American University certifies its commitment to ensuring every college-ready D.C. student has the financial resources, coaching, and community they need to succeed. American University will collaborate closely with DC CAP to maximize financial aid availability, stacking DC CAP scholarships, Pell Grants, D.C. Tuition Assistance Grants (DCTAG), and institutional aid with the goal of helping D.C. students finish college with little to no debt. The partnership will also provide tailored academic and socio-emotional support to D.C. students, from enrollment to graduation.

"For so many of our scholars, staying close to the community they grew up in matters, and having one of the nation's top universities just a short Metro ride away means they don't have to choose between a great education and home," said Eric Waldo, executive director of DC CAP. "We couldn't be more thrilled to be joining forces with American University. This partnership will help turn proximity into opportunity, and ensure that more students in the District can access the support they need to learn and thrive."

Students who are interested in participating in DC CAP programs can confirm their eligibility by taking a short online survey, which opens on October 15, and then applying in January 2027. For more information, please visit www.dccap.org/programs/university-partners.

About the DC College Access Program

The DC College Access Program (DC CAP Scholars) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to eliminating the higher education achievement gap for D.C. students by helping them access and attain meaningful college degrees with little to no debt. DC CAP Scholars believes that a student's personal circumstances should never determine their ability to succeed. By leveraging dollars, connecting students to better match universities, and providing wraparound support, DC CAP Scholars works to ensure students graduate ready to compete in today's economy.

About American University

American University leverages the power and purpose of scholarship, learning, and community to impact our changing world. AU's faculty, students, staff, and alumni shape the future from artificial intelligence to civic life and the sciences. Building on our 133-year history of education and research, AU is committed to addressing the world's pressing issues.

releases.title: Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship for Sciences Announces 2027 Application Cycle for Undergraduate Students Across the USA
releases.body:
SEGUIN, Texas, Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship for Sciences officially opens its application period for the 2027 cycle, inviting undergraduate students nationwide to submit their credentials for consideration.

The scholarship serves as a platform to recognize students who view science not merely as a subject of study, but as a collaborative endeavor with far-reaching societal implications. By providing financial assistance and public recognition, the Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship aims to alleviate some of the burdens associated with higher education, allowing recipients to focus more intently on their research and academic goals.

Eligibility for the award requires applicants to be currently enrolled undergraduate students at an accredited U.S. institution. Candidates must pursue a degree in a science-related field and maintain a strong academic record, evidenced by official transcripts. Additionally, applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

Dr. Kerry Evans brings over two decades of experience in high-pressure medical environments to this philanthropic effort. As a dedicated emergency room physician, he understands the importance of precision, dedication, and continuous learning.

Applicants must submit a 1,000-word essay addressing the specified prompt, official transcripts from their current institution, and letters of recommendation from professors or qualified professionals who can attest to their academic potential. All materials must be sent to apply@drkerryevansscholarship.com by the deadline of May 15, 2027.

The winner of this one-time award will be announced on June 15, 2027. This timeline allows the selection committee ample time to review submissions thoroughly and ensure that the recipient truly embodies the spirit of scientific curiosity and academic diligence.

For those interested in learning more about the requirements or the vision behind the initiative, detailed information is available at https://drkerryevansscholarship.com/.

About the Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship for Sciences

The Dr. Kerry Evans Scholarship for Sciences was established by Dr. Kerry Evans, a seasoned emergency room physician with a deep commitment to education and healthcare advancement. Founded to support undergraduate students pursuing science-related degrees, the organization aims to reduce financial barriers and encourage academic excellence. Its core mission is to inspire the next generation of scientists by recognizing their potential and providing the resources necessary to achieve their professional goals.

releases.title: FaverGray Named a 2026 Best Place to Work by Jacksonville Business Journal
releases.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FaverGray, a general contractor specializing in multifamily and student housing construction, has been named one of the Jacksonville Business Journal's 2026 Best Places to Work, recognizing the company among Northeast Florida employers known for creating strong workplace cultures.

The annual Best Places to Work program recognizes companies throughout the First Coast based on feedback from their employees, with confidential surveys evaluating areas including team dynamics, trust in leadership, communication and overall workplace experience.

For FaverGray, the recognition comes at an exciting time of growth. As the company continues to grow, so does its team, creating new opportunities for employees to advance their careers, take on greater responsibilities and contribute to FaverGray's future.

"Our people have always been the foundation of FaverGray," said James A. Gray, CEO of FaverGray. "As we've grown, we've worked hard to maintain a culture where people enjoy coming to work, feel valued as part of the team and have opportunities to grow with the company. Being recognized as a Best Place to Work is especially meaningful because it comes from the feedback of our own employees."

That culture extends beyond the work itself. FaverGray makes it a priority to bring its team together throughout the year, whether it's a monthly food truck at the Jacksonville Beach office, holiday celebrations, team outings or company events. Most recently, employees and their families spent an afternoon together at Beach Bowl for FaverGray's Family Day, and the team is already looking forward to its annual Chili Cook-Off this fall.

Earlier this year, FaverGray completed an expansion of its Jacksonville Beach headquarters with the team in mind. In addition to new office space, the expansion includes indoor and outdoor gathering areas that have quickly become a favorite place for team lunches, monthly food trucks, celebrations and company events. The new space gives employees a place to step away from their desks, spend time together and celebrate the milestones that make working at FaverGray special.

For FaverGray, these investments are part of maintaining the culture that has been central to the company for more than two decades. As the team grows, the company remains focused on creating opportunities for employees to develop professionally, step into leadership roles and build long-term careers at FaverGray.

"Growth is exciting, but what's equally important to us is making sure FaverGray continues to be a place where people want to come to work and build their careers," said Ben J. Hinson, President of FaverGray. "We want to give our team opportunities to grow professionally, but we also want to make time to get together, celebrate our successes and enjoy the people we work with. Our new office expansion is another investment in that culture and in creating a workplace our team can be proud of."

FaverGray remains headquartered in Jacksonville Beach, where the company was founded in 2005. While its project footprint has grown over the years, Jacksonville Beach remains home and an important part of the company's identity.

FaverGray is among the companies selected by the Jacksonville Business Journal for its 2026 Best Places to Work program. Honorees will be recognized at the Best Places to Work event on November 5, 2026, at the Jacksonville Zoo and Botanical Gardens.

About FaverGray

FaverGray is a general contractor specializing in multifamily and student housing construction throughout the Southeast and beyond. Headquartered in Jacksonville Beach, Florida, the company provides preconstruction and construction services across a range of project types, including garden-style, wrap, podium and mixed-use developments. Since its founding in 2005, FaverGray has built more than 20,000 residential units representing more than $3 billion in construction value. FaverGray is licensed in 19 states and partners with developers across a growing portfolio of markets. For more information, visit favergray.com.

releases.title: TekStream to Spotlight Cybersecurity Workforce Development and Digital Resilience at Educause 2026
releases.body:
Proactive cybersecurity provider to lead sessions on evolving student SOC programs and making cyber risk visible across higher education

ATLANTA, Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TekStream, the digital resilience leader helping organizations modernize, secure and optimize their digital environments, today announced its participation at the 2026 Educause Annual Conference in Denver, CO from Sept. 29 through Oct. 2.

Throughout the conference, TekStream cybersecurity leaders will share practical approaches to two challenges higher education institutions face: building a stronger pipeline of career-ready cybersecurity talent and creating greater visibility into institutional cyber risk. TekStream will lead two sessions focused on helping colleges and universities evolve their security programs while strengthening long-term digital resilience.

"Higher education institutions are being asked to manage increasingly complex cyber environments while also developing the talent needed to protect them," said Taylor Morgan, Chief Solutions Officer at TekStream. "Educause gives us an opportunity to bring those conversations together and share practical models that can help institutions strengthen security today while building the workforce and capabilities they will need tomorrow."

The first of TekStream's two sessions is "Rethinking the Student SOC: Expanding Cyber Workforce Development Beyond Triage," which will take place Wednesday, Sept. 30 from 9:30 – 10:30 am MT. During the session, Matt Clemmons, Managing Director at TekStream, and Bruce Johnson, VP of Solutions Development, will explore how higher education institutions can evolve student security operations center (SOC) programs beyond traditional alert triage. As AI increasingly automates routine security analysis, the session will examine opportunities to expose students to higher-value functions including detection engineering, automation, incident response, risk intelligence, compliance and executive reporting.

On Thursday, Oct. 1, Johnson and Morgan will host the session, "From Blind Spots to Board Insight: Making Cyber Risk Visible in Higher Ed," from 1 – 1:45 pm MT. They'll discuss another persistent challenge for higher education security teams: turning fragmented security data into a clear picture of institutional cyber risk. The session will introduce a practical framework to reduce visibility gaps, establish continuous compliance assurance, and translate operational security data into insights that better inform institutional leaders and boards.

Attendees will leave with actionable approaches to connect technical telemetry to institutional risk, demonstrate the maturity of the security program, and improve cybersecurity decision-making across the institution.

"Higher education has a unique opportunity to make cybersecurity part of both its institutional resilience strategy and its educational mission," said Johnson. "By providing students with meaningful experience beyond alert triage and giving institutional leaders clearer insight into cyber risk, universities can build stronger security programs while preparing the next generation of cybersecurity professionals."

In addition to the conference sessions, TekStream will host a Higher Education Happy Hour on Wednesday, Sept. 30 from 6-8 pm MT at EDGE Restaurant & Bar at Four Seasons Hotel Denver. Educause attendees are invited to connect with TekStream leaders and higher education peers to continue the conversation around cybersecurity, workforce development and digital resilience. Please RSVP at https://go.tekstream.com/TekStreamEducauseFallHH2026 

About TekStream

TekStream is a digital resilience company that helps organizations secure, modernize, and operate their technology environments so they can adapt, recover, and grow. Named a Representative Vendor in the 2025 Gartner® Market Guide for Co-Managed Security Monitoring Services, TekStream delivers cloud migration, Managed Detection and Response (MDR), Security Operations Center (SOC) capabilities, and workforce consulting for commercial and government clients. With more than 200 active customers and a 98% retention rate, TekStream delivers on time and on budget. The company's Whole-of-State cybersecurity model combines workforce development with cost-deferment strategies, empowering public sector organizations to maintain long-term ownership of their security programs.

releases.title: A&M-San Antonio Rises Nine Spots in 2027 U.S. News Social Mobility Rankings

SAN ANTONIO, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Texas A&M University-San Antonio continues to climb in the latest U.S. News & World Report College Rankings, making its largest gain in the Top Performers on Social Mobility category, advancing nine spots to No. 31.

The social mobility ranking measures how successfully universities enroll and graduate students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Approximately 60% of A&M-San Antonio students are Pell Grant-eligible, reflecting the University's mission to expand access to higher education and create pathways to opportunity. Helping drive that impact is Jaguar Promise, which removes financial barriers by covering tuition and fees for eligible Texas students from families earning $70,000 or less. The University's mission also creates wealth for students, as Jaguars receive a cumulative value of $427 million in increased earnings over their working lives.  

The University also rose one spot to No. 28 among Top Public Schools and held steady on its ranking as No. 56 among Regional Universities West, which includes institutions across 14 states, including Texas, Washington, Nevada and California.

"These rankings reflect what happens when a university puts students at the center of everything it does," said President Salvador Hector Ochoa. "Our continued progress in the U.S. News rankings, particularly in social mobility, recognizes our success in creating meaningful pathways to a college degree and greater opportunity. As A&M-San Antonio continues to grow, we remain focused on providing a high-quality education that changes lives, strengthens our community and prepares our students to make an impact in Texas and beyond."

releases.title: The Princeton Review's "Paying for College: 2027 Edition" Is Out
releases.body:
Annually updated guide provides strategies for completing the 2027–2028 FAFSA and CSS Profile to one's best advantage as well as planning for college costs

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Princeton Review®, a provider of education services and college admission resources since 1981, today released the 35th edition of its annual guide to getting funding to pay for college.

Paying for College: Everything You Need to Maximize Financial Aid and Afford College (2027 Edition, Penguin Random House, September 22, 2026, $25.99) is authored by Kalman A. Chany, a nationally recognized expert on college funding, with Geoff Martz. Chany is founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent college financial aid advisory firm based in New York City.

When Paying for College debuted in 1992, it was a one-of-a-kind resource in the category of personal finance guides. It provided detailed line-by-line guidance on strategically completing the two most important financial aid application forms for the upcoming aid application year, and it was the only book to do so.

Paying for College remains the only resource offering such targeted guidance for submitting those two crucial forms. They are the U.S. Department of Education's FAFSA® (Free Application for Federal Student Aid), which all financial aid applicants must submit, and the College Board's CSS Profile®, an application that hundreds of selective colleges require (and which has as many as 200 questions).

"You might think that families who receive the most financial aid would be the families with the most need," Chany says in the introduction of the book. "In fact, this is not necessarily true. The people who receive the most aid are the people who best understand the aid process." 

Chany well understands the process. Since 1981, he has annually analyzed the major aid application forms as well as the formulas by which federal and institutional financial aid administrators assess an applicant's need for aid based on answers on the forms. He guides his clients (and readers of this book) on how to maximize their eligibility for financial aid much in the same way an accountant advises clients on submitting their IRS returns to their best advantage. (All the strategies Chany recommends follow the law to the letter.)

In Paying for College, Chany also covers other subjects important to aid applicants and parents, including how to:

  • explore long- and short-term strategies for reducing college costs
  • research colleges with financial aid in mind
  • compare financial aid offers and, if necessary, appeal for more aid
  • obtain education loans, understand payment plans, and manage loan debt

A Special Topics chapter in the book gives particular advice on aid applications for parents who are single, separated, divorced or in blended families as well as advice for students who are independent, international or older than the traditional applicant.

The 2027 edition of Paying for College also reports on tectonic changes that have impacted the college funding landscape as a result of various provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) signed into law in July 2025. Chany discusses what parents and students need to know about these changes. Icons in the margins flag topics that were pending as the book went to press that readers are advised to check.

Some provisions of the OBBBA that impact federal student aid are still unresolved. "Unfortunately," Chany notes, "some guidance involving federal education loans issued by the U.S. Department of Education is being misinterpreted—even by college aid professionals."

Over the years, Paying for College has been praised by reviewers and finance professionals alike. Forbes contributor John Wasik noted it "can save thousands in college bills." Washington Post syndicated columnist Michelle Singletary chose it for her Color of Money book club. Newsday Family Finance columnist Lynn Brenner recommended it as "a first-rate guide through the financial aid maze."

Said Rob Franek, Editor-in-Chief of The Princeton Review, "Our company has a deep appreciation for the concerns of students and parents about paying for college. Among nearly 10,000 college applicants and parents of applicants who completed our 2026 College Hopes & Worries Survey in February, 93% reported they would need financial aid to pay for college, and 81% of that cohort characterized their level of need as "very" or "extremely" necessary. We hope the advice in this new edition of Paying for College will help parents and students apply strategies to get all the financial aid they are entitled to and enable them to pay less for college."

Paying for College is one of more than 150 books developed by The Princeton Review and published by Penguin Random House in a line that includes The Best 392 Colleges  and guides to the SAT®, ACT®, and AP® exams. The Princeton Review is also known for its annual college rankings in dozens of categories including its popular "Great Financial Aid" college ranking list and its "Best Value Colleges" lists.

About Kalman A. Chany 

Kalman A. Chany is the founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent New York City-based financial aid advisory firm. For more than four decades, his firm has helped thousands of families maximize their financial aid eligibility and save tens of thousands of dollars off the cost of their children's college education. Kal has been sourced in The Wall Street Journal, on CNBC, and in Money magazine, and he has appeared on CBS Evening News, NBC Nightly News, and other broadcast media.

About The Princeton Review

The Princeton Review is a leading tutoring, test prep, and college admissions services company. Every year, it helps millions of college- and graduate school–bound students as well as working professionals achieve their education and career goals through its many education services and products. These include online and in-person courses delivered by a network of more than 4,000 teachers and tutors; online resources; a line of more than 150 print and digital books published by Penguin Random House; and dozens of categories of school rankings. Founded in 1981, the company is now in its 45th year. The company's Tutor.com brand, now in its 25th year, is one of the largest online tutoring services in the U.S. It comprises a community of thousands of tutors who have delivered more than 29 million tutoring sessions. The Princeton Review, headquartered in New York, NY, is not affiliated with Princeton University. For more information, visit PrincetonReview.com. Follow the company on Facebook (@ThePrincetonReviewSAT), Instagram (@theprincetonreview), LinkedIn (the-princeton-review), YouTube (@ThePrincetonReview), and TikTok (@princeton.review). releases.summary: BUFFALO, N.Y., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BetterMynd, a leading online therapy platform centered on the mental health needs of university and college students, has announced a partnership with Lavender Psychiatry, the largest nurse-led online psychiatry and therapy practice in the United States. Together, the organizations will expand access to flexible, high-quality care by integrating Lavender's medication management services into the BetterMynd therapeutic ecosystem.
releases.title: BetterMynd & Lavender Collaborate To Improve Mental Health Resources for College and University Students
releases.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BetterMynd, a leading online therapy platform centered on the mental health needs of university and college students, has announced a partnership with Lavender Psychiatry, the largest nurse-led online psychiatry and therapy practice in the United States. Together, the organizations will expand access to flexible, high-quality care by integrating Lavender's medication management services into the BetterMynd therapeutic ecosystem.

With one in three students reporting symptoms of moderate anxiety or depression (Healthy Minds, 2025), the demand for accessible care is at an all-time high. This partnership reflects a shared belief that students are best served by adaptable care models built around the individual. By combining their expertise, BetterMynd and Lavender can better respond to the full spectrum of mental health needs seen across the student population.

For educational institutions navigating growing demand and increasing complexity in student mental health, the partnership offers a high-quality, scalable solution that is easy to implement.

"Our mission is to make getting help easier for every college student, and we believe every student deserves an exceptional experience," said Cody Semrau, Founder and CEO of BetterMynd. "We're excited to partner with Lavender, an organization that shares our mission-driven focus and also puts the students first in all that they do. This ensures students have the most comprehensive resources available while providing institutions with a trusted, scalable model."

Accessing psychiatric care can often mean navigating long wait times, referrals between multiple providers, and limited prescribing options; barriers that can be especially challenging for student populations. Lavender removes this friction by providing integrated psychiatric services within BetterMynd's established care pathway, from assessment and prescribing to ongoing medication management, including ADHD treatment and controlled substances when clinically appropriate. With virtual appointments typically available within one week, students can get the support they need without lengthy delays. A network of 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across more than 40 states, supported by customized referral pathways and dedicated administrative support, helps make that access seamless and scalable for BetterMynd's university partners.

"We believe in creating a world where feelings are respected and cared for. BetterMynd shares our passion for making kind, effective, high-quality care more accessible," said Pritma Dhillon-Chattha, DNP, MHA, RN, Co-Founder of Lavender. "Mental health journeys are unique and we're reflecting that in our joint adaptable approach to therapy and medication management. By embedding Lavender's online psychiatry services naturally into the BetterMynd community, we're making the student journey more seamless and serving as a true extension of the campus counseling center."

The partnership is currently live at select institutions. Both organizations will continue to build and expand access across multiple states and campuses throughout 2026 and beyond.

About BetterMynd

BetterMynd is a leading online therapy platform designed specifically to meet the mental health needs of college students. BetterMynd supplements and expands on-campus resources by providing personalized care and scheduling flexibility. Serving more than 100 colleges and universities, BetterMynd reaches over 500,000 students through a network of 400+ licensed clinicians. Learn more at www.bettermynd.com.

About Lavender

Lavender Psychiatry is the largest nurse-owned and operated online psychiatry and therapy office in the U.S. Founded on the principle that care should be kind, collaborative and effective, Lavender provides timely access to high-quality therapy and medication management through 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across 40+ states. The practice also works with partners by integrating select services into existing mental health care ecosystems. Learn more at www.joinlavender.com.

releases.title: Disasterville Returns: Army National Guard Brings Mixed-Reality Disaster Response Missions Back to Schools
releases.body:
At a Glance

  • This fall, the U.S. Army National Guard's mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, is returning to high schools nationwide to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies. 
  • Disasterville guides students through high-tech, virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes in the same way as the Guard.
  • The Disasterville tour continues to introduce students to the possibilities available in the Army National Guard—a unique component within the U.S. Army where Soldiers have the flexibility to serve their country part-time while also pursuing a civilian career or higher education. 

WASHINGTON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This fall, the Army National Guard's immersive mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, will begin its second nationwide tour of high schools, giving students a first-hand look at how to prepare for and respond to natural disasters—without leaving their schools. Disasterville is activating in high school gyms where it will take students through virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes, just like Soldiers responding to similar emergencies in communities across the country. This follows Disasterville's successful inaugural tour in spring 2026, which reached more than 2,000 students.

"Natural disasters are not slowing down, and Army National Guard Soldiers are playing a critical role in response efforts across the country," says Lt. Col. Sabrina Zowada, Chief of the National Guard Bureau's Marketing and Advertising Branch. "Disasterville is a one-of-a-kind perspective for students to see how and when the Guard is showing up in their communities, and experience the real skills and impact of these important missions." 

Disasterville is transforming high school gyms from September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga.

Students Work Together to Respond to Common Missions

Disasterville uses advanced mixed-reality technology to create three 10-minute missions most common to Army National Guard response efforts. Working together in teams of five, students are called to service at the following sites:

  • Wildfire: Amid a raging wildfire, teams work together to push back fires encroaching on a home in Disaster Canyon. Students will put out small wildfires, combine forces to push back larger flare-ups, save animals, and dodge falling trees. 
  • Flood Zone: After a major hurricane, civilians are fighting to stay above water on the streets they call home. Students will board their Zodiac and use headlamps to find and safely evacuate survivors while avoiding dangerous wildlife and other lurking hazards.
  • Earthquake: After a devastating earthquake, a train carrying hazardous chemicals and passengers derails, pinning civilians and spilling dangerous material, poisoning the air. Time ticks down as students arm themselves with the jaws of life to rescue survivors and clean up debris, all before the train gives way under its own weight.

"We saw firsthand how students connected with the Disasterville experience. They didn't just learn about disaster response—they felt the responsibility," says Lt. Col. Zawada. "Today's young people want purpose; they want action, and they want to know how they can contribute to something meaningful. We're excited to show even more students how the Guard meets that need."

Mixed-Reality Technology Brings Immersion and Impact

Disasterville utilizes advanced mixed-reality technology with augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) graphics mapped to large plywood structures, creating a free-roam virtual neighborhood experience in high school gyms. Students wear virtual reality headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, and hazards, rescuing people in need. The technology also features advanced hand tracking, eliminating the need for game controllers and allowing students to interact with others and physically use in-game props and Army National Guard rescue tools like oars, hoses, chainsaws, and the jaws of life.  

Extended reality (XR) industry expert Dale Carman helped the Army bring the Disasterville experience to life. Carman is the co-founder and executive creative director at Groove Jones, which has over 25 years of experience in feature films, immersive tech, and branded productions.

A specialized tour crew will be present at each tour stop to guide participants safely through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about service.   

For more information on the Army National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

Supplementary Information

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is Disasterville, and how does the experience work?

A: Disasterville is a mixed-reality experience from the U.S. Army National Guard touring the nation, transforming gymnasiums into full-scale, mission-oriented disaster zones to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies through hands-on simulations. Students wear Meta Quest 3 headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, hazards, and people in need. Students are guided firsthand through high-tech, virtual missions, working together in teams to tackle three disaster zones -- wildfire, flood zone, and earthquake -- the same way as the Guard, by combining communication, physical endurance, and ingenuity to save lives, landscape, and their communities.

Q: Where will Disasterville be traveling?

A: Following a successful 2026 spring tour, Disasterville will head to even more high schools September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga. At each tour stop, a specialized tour crew will ensure the safety of and guide participants through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about Guard service.   

Q: What do Army National Guard Soldiers do? Where and how do they serve?

A: With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers serve part-time to support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Serving at least one weekend a month and two weeks a year, National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to pursue their civilian personal and professional passions.

Q: Where can I learn more about opportunities in the Army National Guard?

A: For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

About the Army National Guard (ARNG):

With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Army National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to serve part-time across medical, aviation, law enforcement, transportation, and engineering fields and beyond, while also pursuing their personal and professional goals through a civilian career or higher education. For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

releases.title: Get There: FLORIDA ANNOUNCES THE START OF WORKFORCE PELL GRANT FUNDING TO SUPPORT SHORT-TERM, CAREER-FOCUSED TRAINING
releases.body:
TALLAHASSEE, Fla., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, Governor Ron DeSantis announced Florida's initial list of eligible short-term workforce programs for purposes of implementing the new federal Workforce Pell Grant program. This program is a Trump Administration priority and provides federal financial aid to students enrolled in short-term workforce training programs that lead directly to employment in high-skill, high-wage, or in-demand occupations.

Aligned with state workforce demand, the Workforce Pell Grant supports students' continued education and career advancement while strengthening the state's workforce pipeline. Workforce Pell eligible programs must prepare students for occupations that demonstrate strong labor market demand or fulfill critical workforce needs within Florida's economy and communities.

"Florida is number one in workforce education, and the Workforce Pell Grant funding enables us to build on our track record of success," said Governor Ron DeSantis. "The programs eligible for Workforce Pell funding are preparing students for high-wage, in-demand careers. We're glad that thousands more Floridians will be able to take advantage of these opportunities without needing to take out loans or break the bank."

Governor Ron DeSantis has delegated Commissioner of Education Henry Mack to lead the statewide implementation of the Workforce Pell Grant. The Florida Department of Education is using the Targeted Occupations List managed by FloridaCommerce and the CareerSource Florida Master Credential List to determine eligible programs.

"By prioritizing short-term workforce training that allows students to earn a credential in as little as 8 weeks, the Workforce Pell Grant helps students earn the skills they need to enter the workforce with little to no debt," said Commissioner of Education Henry Mack. "The programs identified as eligible for Workforce Pell funding are within high-wage and in-demand industries, ensuring students will be able to find fulfilling careers after completing their programs."

Under Governor DeSantis' leadership, Florida has been named the nation's number one state for workforce education, and the Workforce Pell Grant further showcases his commitment to workforce education, adding to the $12 billion already committed during his administration.

For more information about Florida's implementation of the Workforce Pell Grant and to view the inventory of eligible programs, visit www.fldoe.org/workforcepell.

For more information about the Florida Department of Education, visit www.fldoe.org.
